entries.clue: This puzzle’s toppers for 28 occur a couple of ways (5)

blocks.note: to be = to exist, to occur
two compass directions, north and south

annotation.surface: A setter boasting that the toast in this grid comes with a topping served twice over.
annotation.walkthrough: The theme: each bean in the grid (FLAGEOLET, GREEN, RUNNER, JUMPING, BEANS itself) sits directly above a drinking toast (SLAINTE, PROSIT, SKOAL, BOTTOMS UP), so 28's TOAST comes both ways, the breakfast and the raised glass.
annotation.definitionFit: Beans on toast is the classic British snack, so beans are what tops toast, and in this grid they literally sit on top of the toasts.

entries.clue: Cross new wife gripping groom's head (6)

indicatorNotes.gripping: the new wife holds the letter in her grip, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a bride is a newly married woman

annotation.surface: A newly-wed bride, annoyed, clutching her husband's head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, the bride's mood; it is the verb, to span. The G slips in just before the bride's last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to span a river or gap, as a bridge does.

entries.clue: Online program always reflected fruitful growth (5,4)

indicatorNotes.reflected: a reflection shows a word back to front

blocks.note: an applet is a small program run in a web page

annotation.surface: A tech review praising an app that has kept growing steadily.
annotation.walkthrough: E'ER for 'always' is a crossword staple from poetry; turned round it gives REE.
annotation.definitionFit: An apple tree grows and bears fruit, so it is literally fruitful growth.

entries.clue: Films provided to occupy relative (7)

indicatorNotes.to occupy: one word moves into the other and fills its middle

annotation.surface: Someone lending money so a relative can take a lease.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Films' in the plural is the whole definition: early cinema without soundtracks, known collectively by the adjective turned noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Silents are silent films, the pictures made before sound.

entries.clue: ELO perhaps changes direction, inspired by detuned flute (9)

indicatorNotes.changes direction: the letters run the other way
indicatorNotes.inspired by: breathed in by the outer word, so held inside it

annotation.surface: A band that swaps musical style after hearing a badly tuned flute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'ELO perhaps' looks like a band given as an example; 'perhaps' is only the abbreviation for 'for example'. ELO is the rock band Electric Light Orchestra, used purely for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small fipple flute, like a tin whistle; it is also a bean, which is why it sits over SLAINTE.

entries.clue: Lost backing and received double-digit sum (9)

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: to be for something is to back it
ten is the first number with two digits

annotation.surface: A gambler who lost their stake but took home ten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'backing' does its own work here: FOR = in favour of, backing. TEN is the smallest two-digit number.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of gone from memory, as a forgotten name is a lost one.

entries.clue: Fools common folks out of millions (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: the M is taken out of the word

annotation.surface: Ordinary people cheated out of millions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fools' looks like the verb, to con people out of money; it is the plural noun. (M)ASSES.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the donkey's reputation for stupidity makes an ass a byword for a fool.

entries.clue: Time before inevitable cancellation (7)

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

annotation.surface: The period before an event is inevitably called off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'before' just puts ERA first.
annotation.definitionFit: An erasure is a deletion, the cancelling of something written.

entries.clue: Discovered in Whitechapel: an airy veranda? (5)

indicatorNotes.Discovered in: the answer is found inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: An open-air porch turning up in an unlikely part of East London.
annotation.walkthrough: Whitechapel is a crowded area of East London, the last place for an airy veranda, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A lanai is a Hawaiian veranda or open-sided porch.

entries.clue: Even you would like hippie clothing (3-4)

annotation.definitionNote: TIE-DYED is an adjective; the definition reads as a noun phrase, the look of the clothing

blocks.note: ye'd = you would, with the old ye

annotation.surface: Someone saying that even you would fancy the hippie look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb ('even you'); it is the adjective, level, as in scores.
annotation.definitionFit: Tie-dyed shirts, patterned by knotting and dyeing, are the classic hippie garment.

entries.clue: Thing puncturing another – one's lighter (7)

annotation.surface: A cryptic label on a sharp object that seems to be about a cigarette lighter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'one's lighter' suggests a lighter belonging to someone; read it as I'M PALER, one (I) is (M) lighter.
annotation.definitionFit: An impaler is something that pierces another thing right through.

entries.clue: Tribute done in empty template (7)

indicatorNotes.empty: emptied of its middle, leaving just the outside letters

annotation.surface: A tribute written on a blank form.
annotation.walkthrough: 'done in' looks like 'filled in', matching the template; it means killed.
annotation.definitionFit: Slainte is the Gaelic toast ('health'), a tribute raised with a glass.

entries.clue: Party on, in general (5)

indicatorNotes.in: one word goes in the other

annotation.surface: Someone telling a crowd to keep partying, in a vague way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'broadly'; 'general' is shortened, as army ranks are in print, and 'on' is the memo-header 'regarding'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Greens are an environmentalist political party.

entries.clue: Vagueness by court is misrepresented (9)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, in a new order

annotation.surface: A complaint that a judgment's vagueness has been distorted by the court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like the institution doing the misrepresenting; it is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: writing that is hard to make out is unclear, the fault of meaning both words name.

entries.clue: Experts with lovemaking: here's how (6)

annotation.surface: A sex manual promising expert instruction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'here's how' pretends to open an explanation; it is an old drinking toast, like 'cheers'.
annotation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin toast, meaning 'may it benefit'; 'here's how' is an old English toast.

entries.clue: Guard largely was familiar with recording commercial (7)

indicatorNotes.largely: most of the word, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: KNEW, 'was familiar with', minus its W

annotation.surface: A security guard who mostly knew about a record and an advert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like part of 'familiar with'; KNEW alone is 'was familiar', and 'with' joins the next pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A kneepad is protective padding, a guard for the knee.

entries.clue: How to manage shock? Drink through gallons then rest well (5,4)

blocks.note: kir = white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

annotation.surface: Advice for coping with a shock: have a stiff drink, then sleep it off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a fright; it is a shock of hair. A kirby grip is the British name for a bobby pin.
annotation.definitionFit: A kirby grip holds unruly hair in place, so it is how to manage a shock of hair.

entries.clue: Remarkable people elevated plant and brand making brown sauce (9)

indicatorNotes.elevated: raised up; in a down answer the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: HP Sauce is the best-known British brown sauce

annotation.surface: Celebrities raising a plant and launching a brown-sauce label.
annotation.walkthrough: Brown sauce is a tangy British condiment eaten with a fry-up; HP is its best-known brand.
annotation.definitionFit: A phenomenon is also a person of outstanding ability, a prodigy; the plural covers several such people.

entries.clue: Composer mixed up lines and space (7)

indicatorNotes.mixed up: things mixed up are jumbled out of their proper order, so the letters of the word come out rearranged

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space

annotation.surface: A composer who has muddled his staff lines and gaps.
annotation.walkthrough: An en (like an em) is a unit of space in printing, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was the Danish composer of six symphonies.

entries.clue: Surgery twisted bones to save pair of joints (4,3)

indicatorNotes.twisted: the letters are bent out of order
indicatorNotes.to save: the anagram keeps the other piece safe inside it
indicatorNotes.pair of: the first two letters of the next word

annotation.surface: An orthopaedic operation on broken bones, sparing two joints.
annotation.walkthrough: The bones-and-joints surface points to orthopaedics; the surgery is cosmetic. NOSE(JO)B.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal name for rhinoplasty, the cosmetic operation reshaping a nose.

entries.clue: Mute very Republican old lizard (7)

annotation.surface: A description of a silent, old-guard Republican politician as a dinosaur.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mute' reads as silent; it is the noun, the device that damps an instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A sordino is a mute for a stringed or brass instrument.

entries.clue: One dashing leader? (6)

blocks.note: one who runs things, as a showrunner leads a TV series

annotation.surface: A leader who is also handsome and stylish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'dashing' looks like handsome; it is running.
annotation.definitionFit: A runner is someone who dashes; someone who runs an organisation leads it.

entries.clue: Developing perfume across the pond? (7)

blocks.note: NA = North America, over the Atlantic from Britain

annotation.surface: A fragrance being developed in America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' is British slang for America across the Atlantic; here it gives NA. The question mark flags the loose clueing.
annotation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, still developing.

entries.clue: Stew contains left over bit of broccoli (6)

annotation.surface: A stew with a leftover piece of broccoli in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stew' and 'left over' paint a kitchen; STEW is the verb, to worry. F(LO)RET.
annotation.definitionFit: Broccoli's head breaks into small clustered flower-heads, each one of these being a single piece.

entries.clue: Short attendant at bank, bright-eyed and bushy-tailed? (9)

indicatorNotes.Short: cut short, the last letter goes

blocks.note: SQUIRE, a knight's attendant, minus its E
to bank on = to rely on

annotation.surface: A short bank clerk who is lively and eager.
annotation.walkthrough: 'bright-eyed and bushy-tailed' is an idiom for alert and eager; the question mark says take it literally too, like a squirrel.
annotation.definitionFit: Squirrely means squirrel-like, and a squirrel is literally bright-eyed and bushy-tailed.

entries.clue: Peacekeepers and police force not satisfied (5)

annotation.surface: Peacekeepers and police left dissatisfied.
annotation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a demand or target left unfulfilled, as in 'the conditions were never met'.

entries.clue: Creeps pollarded growths around garden (5)

indicatorNotes.pollarded: a pollarded tree has its top cut off, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: hedges grow round a garden; H removed

annotation.surface: Pests crawling through trimmed hedges around a garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Creeps' reads as unpleasant people; it is the verb, edges forward.
annotation.definitionFit: To edge is to move slowly and carefully, to creep.

entries.clue: Southern Aussie native curtailed barroom shout (5)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: its tail cut off, the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A cry in a bar from someone from the south of Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aussie native' looks like a person; it is the koala.
annotation.definitionFit: Skoal is a Scandinavian drinking toast, shouted in a bar.

entries.clue: Judge American officiating pole vault activity (7)

annotation.surface: A US judge officiating at an athletics meet.
annotation.walkthrough: To ump, short for umpire, is chiefly American usage, hence 'American'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the vaulter clears a high bar, one of athletics' leaping events.

entries.clue: Animal sounds like a distraught Scooby-Doo's cry? (3,4)

indicatorNotes.sounds like: says outright that the answer is heard

blocks.note: 'oh dear' in Scooby-Doo's R-heavy dog voice

annotation.surface: A cartoon dog, upset, crying out like some creature.
annotation.walkthrough: Scooby-Doo, the cartoon Great Dane, starts his words with R ('Ruh-roh'), so his 'oh dear' is 'Roh dear'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small woodland species of Europe and Asia.

entries.clue: Small saying in tavern when it's knocked back (7,2)

annotation.definition: Small saying in tavern when it's knocked back

indicatorNotes.in: the pieces go inside the tavern
indicatorNotes.knocked back: sent back, so the whole thing is read right to left

annotation.surface: A little phrase heard in a pub as a drink goes down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' does double duty: drinking a glass down, and sending the letters backwards. Read whole, the clue also defines: a short saying heard in a pub as a drink goes down.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Bottoms up' is said as a drink is downed, the glass's bottom tipped up.

entries.clue: Add wraps as part of fry-up (5)

annotation.surface: Instructions for adding wraps to a cooked breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'wraps' looks like the tortilla food, fitting the breakfast; it is the container instruction. 'Add' is the verb as in 'tot up a bill'.
annotation.definitionFit: Toast is a standard part of a full English fry-up breakfast.
